pr_title: fix: fix pivot when multiple columns are passed. Output is now aligned with what tidyverse / pandas.pivot_table would do
pr_body:
closes #11663 
closes #13120 

WIP, but this has been a longstanding issue, so I get killed while cycling today then hopefully someone can pick up where I left off (UPDATE: all good, made it back safely)

This is _much_ easier to review ignoring whitespace: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/pull/14048/files?w=1

---

todo:
- [x] double-check that, for all these tests and examples I've updated, tidyverse output would match

---

This is probably one of the most satisfying PRs I've ever worked on. One of those cases when the solution isn't to fix the naming strategy, but instead to take a step back and think about what should really be happening when multiple columns are specified
pr_comments: I am going to tag this as a bug fix as multi-column pivots was broken.

issue_context.title: .pivot panics when using a column containing Structs
issue_context.body:
### Checks - [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported. - [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars. ### Reproducible example ```python import polars as pl df = pl.DataFrame( { "index": [1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3], "item_type": ["a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "b"], "item_id": [123, 123, 123, 456, 456, 456], "values": [4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9], } ) df = df.with_columns(pl.struct(["item_type", "item_id"]).alias("columns")).drop("item_type", "item_id") df = df.pivot(index="index", columns="columns", values="values") # this panics ``` ### Log output ```shell run StackExec run UdfExec thread '' panicked at crates/polars-ops/src/frame/pivot/positioning.rs:145:25: assertion failed: idx < buf.len() note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace 9.27s - Error processing internal command. Traceback (most recent call last): File "/home/ubuntu/.vscode-server/extensions/ms-python.python-2023.22.1/pythonFiles/lib/python/debugpy/_vendored/pydevd/pydevd.py", line 1783, in eval_result = pydevd_vars.evaluate_expression(py_db, frame, expression, is_exec=False) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File _run_with_unblock_threads(original_func, py_db, curr_thread, frame, expression, is_exec) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File _run_with_interrupt_thread(original_func, py_db, curr_thread, frame, expression, is_exec) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/home/ubuntu/.vscode-server/extensions/ms-python.python-2023.22.1/pythonFiles/lib/python/debugpy/_vendored/pydevd/_pydevd_bundle/pydevd_vars.py", line 305, in _run_with_interrupt_thread return original_func(py_db, frame, expression, is_exec) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/home/ubuntu/.vscode-server/extensions/ms-python.python-2023.22.1/pythonFiles/lib/python/debugpy/_vendored/pydevd/_pydevd_bundle/pydevd_vars.py", line 580, in evaluate_expression ret = eval_in_context(expression, updated_globals, updated_locals, py_db) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/home/ubuntu/.vscode-server/extensions/ms-python.python-2023.22.1/pythonFiles/lib/python/debugpy/_vendored/pydevd/_pydevd_bundle/pydevd_vars.py", line 268, in eval_in_context result = eval(compiled, global_vars, local_vars) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "", line 1, in File "/home/ubuntu/repos/polars/py-polars/polars/dataframe/frame.py", line 7322, in pivot self._df.pivot_expr( pyo3_runtime.PanicException: assertion failed: idx < buf.len() ``` ### Issue description I am not expecting the pivot operation to panic here - see section below for the output I would expect. I've done some debugging to try to pinpoint where the error comes from: 1 - Rust ```assertion failed: idx < buf.len()``` panic occurs here: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/crates/polars-ops/src/frame/pivot/positioning.rs#L145 2 - ```buf``` is initialised here: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/crates/polars-ops/src/frame/pivot/positioning.rs#L110 and inspection of the variables when running the code using the reproducible example's dataframe shows that on this line```n_cols=2``` and ```n_rows=3``` giving ```buf.len()=6```, which are all correct. 3 - The issue comes from ```col_locations``` here: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/crates/polars-ops/src/frame/pivot/positioning.rs#L131 which instead of being```[0,0,0,1,1,1]``` as I would expect it to be based on the content of the column ```columns``` of the reproducible examples's dataframe, incorrectly is ```[0,1,2,3,4,5]```. This makes ```col_idx``` take values it shouldn't be taking and induces ```idx``` to be larger than ```buf.len()``` in this for loop here: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/crates/polars-ops/src/frame/pivot/positioning.rs#L136-L144 4 - ```col_locations``` is created here: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/crates/polars-ops/src/frame/pivot/positioning.rs#L216-L219 where each ```v``` in the iteration seems distinct -which shouldn't be the case, there are 6 elements iterated over, which should take only 2 distinct values- and thus considered a new entry of ```col_to_idx``` at each iteration yielding the incorrect ```col_locations``` with value ```[0,1,2,3,4,5]```. This problem is not occurring when the column ```columns``` contains eg integers or &str instead of structs. I attempted to look into how ```column_agg_physical``` is created using ```to_physical_repr``` and what's happening in ```phys_iter``` but I am new to rust and polars and I felt like I was reaching the limit of my debugging setup (VSCode + CodeLLDB which is not so great to inspect variables). ________________________________________________________ PS: Just before I forget to mention it in case it turns out important: when initially running into this bug with my actual data, the pivot operation did not systematically panic but the bug seemed to arise at random. With the example above the bug arises 'almost' systematically, but still happened that running in a notebook, the pivot operation did not panic but returned instead an incorrect result: PS2: the documentation of ```to_physical_repr``` details the behaviour for all inputs types except for Struct https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/crates/polars-core/src/series/mod.rs#L439-L440. PS3: To give some context as to why I have been trying to use structs with pivot: coming from pandas, I was quite a keen user of multiindexes, one of the example usage being like the below which I was somehow trying to replicate in polars - pivotting the dataframe with some (date) index in rows and applying eg ffill or whatever time-related transformation to each column: ### Expected behavior ### Installed versions
``` --------Version info--------- Polars: 0.20.0 Index type: UInt32 Platform: Linux-6.2.0-1016-aws-x86_64-with-glibc2.35 Python: 3.11.6 (main, Oct 25 2023, 13:46:41) [GCC 11.4.0] ----Optional dependencies---- adbc_driver_manager: cloudpickle: connectorx: deltalake: fsspec: gevent: matplotlib: numpy: openpyxl: pandas: pyarrow: pydantic: pyiceberg: pyxlsb: sqlalchemy: xlsx2csv: xlsxwriter: ```

review_comments: We use `downcast_iter` so that we get fast iteration and the compiler sees the underlying arrays.
this comment comes from https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/pull/3199/files, but I think it's no longer relevant as there's now a variable called `row_locations` as it's clear what it is

This matches the tidyverse output:
```
select(df, c(A, B, C, D, breaky)) %>% pivot_wider(values_from=D, names_from = c(C, breaky), values_fn = sum)
```
```
# A tibble: 4 × 7
  A     B     small_jam large_egg small_egg large_jam small_potato
  <chr> <chr>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>        <dbl>
1 foo   one           1         4        NA        NA           NA
2 foo   two           3        NA         3        NA           NA
3 bar   one          NA        NA        NA         4            5
4 bar   two           6        NA        NA         7           NA
```
instead of treating each column independently, they're now all grouped over together. so, the extra `{sep}{column_column_name}` doesn't add anything anymore other than verbosity, and can be removed

This matches the tidyverse output:
```
select(df, c(A, B, C, D, breaky)) %>% pivot_wider(values_from=D, names_from = c(C, breaky), values_fn = sum)
```

```
  <chr> <chr>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>        <dbl>
1 foo   one           1         4        NA        NA           NA

3 bar   one          NA        NA        NA         4            5
```

We use `downcast_iter` so that we get fast iteration and the compiler sees the underlying arrays.
instead of treating each column independently, they're now all grouped over together. so, the extra `{sep}{column_column_name}` doesn't add anything anymore other than verbosity, and can be removed
